title: True random number generator: ring-oscillator noise source, SP 800-90B repetition count and adaptive proportion health tests with start-up test, and SHA-256 conditioning into 256-bit full-entropy seeds

regs.name: CTRL
regs.desc: Enable and configuration (src_sel, cond_bypass and cond_blks are taken when en rises)

fields.desc: 1 runs the start-up test, then collection; 0 stops and clears the buffers (and is how a failure is cleared)
noise source: 0 the ring oscillators, 1 the test LFSR (bring-up only: deterministic, no entropy)
1 outputs the raw bits unconditioned, 32 per word, for characterization

regs.name: HEALTH
regs.desc: Health test cutoffs (apply at once); the reset values are those of a claimed min-entropy of 0.5 bit per sample at alpha = 2^-20

fields.desc: repetition count test: a run of this many equal samples fails (1 + ceil(20 / H))

regs.name: ENT
regs.desc: Entropy output: a seed is eight words, digest word 0 first (one word per raw-bit word in bypass); reading ENT pops the word

regs.desc: Health test failures since reset (saturating at 255)

features: Noise source: the XOR of NRO free-running ring oscillators (asynchronous inputs ro_in, placed outside the core) through a two-flop synchronizer, sampled every smp_div + 1 clocks. Every raw sample is also on raw_valid / raw_bit (pass-through pins) for the SP 800-90B entropy assessment and an external monitor.

SP 800-90B health tests on every raw sample: the repetition count test and the adaptive proportion test (1024-sample window), with programmable cutoffs. A start-up test runs one full window before anything is collected; a failure at any time stops the core, raises ALERT and clears the buffers until en is cleared and set again.

Conditioning with SHA-256, a vetted function: 512 x (cond_blks + 1) raw bits per 256-bit seed (1024 by default), each seed from fresh samples. Output as eight words through ENT, with the core held off (no loss) while ENT is full.
Test LFSR source and raw bypass for bring-up and characterization; output from either is never flagged FIPS (STATUS.es_fips, core port ent_fips).
Monitors: failure counters per test since reset and high-water marks (longest run, highest window count) since the last start.
notes: The health test reset values assume 0.5 bit of min-entropy per raw sample. Measure the real source (raw_valid / raw_bit, or bypass words through ENT) with the SP 800-90B tools and set HEALTH, CTRL.smp_div and CTRL.cond_blks from the assessed entropy: 256 + 64 bits of entropy must go into each seed for full entropy.

The ring oscillators are not part of the core: a production design places NRO oscillators of different lengths in the analog / custom area, with their enables; ro_in is their output. In simulation the testbench drives them from a noise model.

Not implemented: an SP 800-90A DRBG on top (the seeds feed one, or the Root_of_Trust UDS / key generation); oscillator enables and frequency monitors; side-channel and fault-injection hardening beyond the state register check.
sequence: Configure: HEALTH = rct_cutoff | apt_cutoff << 8 (or keep the reset values), CTRL = cond_blks << 3 | smp_div << 5 with en = 0.
Start: set CTRL.en; STATUS.state goes 1 (START) then 2 (RUN) once 1024 samples have passed.
Read a seed: wait for IRQ_STATUS.SEED (or FLAGS ENT available), then read ENT eight times (digest word 0 first).
On IRQ_STATUS.ALERT: read STATUS (alert_rct / alert_apt) and FAILS, clear CTRL.en, then set it again to rerun the start-up test.
verification: Core: tb/TRNG_tb.sv drives the ring oscillator inputs from a noise model (random, stuck, runs of ones and zeros) and reads with random back-pressure. Its own model runs both health tests on every raw sample and predicts each failure, flag, counter and high-water mark; it hashes the samples each seed is made of with its own SHA-256 (first checked against hashlib vectors from scripts/trng/gen_vec.py) and compares every output word. Cases: every block count, both sources, bypass, sampling every clock to every 256 clocks, each test failing in START, RUN, HASH and OUT, cutoffs of 0 and 1, both tests at once, counter saturation, en dropped in every state, reset mid-output.

The core checker is a separate cycle model from the ports (synchronizer, LFSR, divider, health tests, control timing) with its own SHA-256 (constants from the primes); it checks every raw sample, state, flag, counter and output word, and that no sample data is left in the buffers when the core is not collecting.
